name: Data Analyzer: Web page start script turns on cross-site request protections by default
objective: Proves the start script enables XSRF and CORS protection (browser safeguards against forged or cross-site requests) when nothing is configured.
precondition: The container start script entrypoint.sh is run in a temporary folder with fake 'python' and 'streamlit' programs; the fake streamlit just prints the options it was given.

steps.action: Run the start script with no settings
steps.expected: The streamlit options include --server.enableXsrfProtection=true and --server.enableCORS=true

name: Data Analyzer: A deployed container cannot switch the protections off
objective: Proves the local-only override is ignored when the setup looks deployed.
precondition: The container start script entrypoint.sh is run in a temporary folder with fake 'python' and 'streamlit' programs; the fake streamlit just prints the options it was given.

steps.action: Run the start script with STREAMLIT_INSECURE_LOCAL_ONLY=1 plus a deployed marker
steps.expected: In both cases the options still say XSRF protection and CORS are true, and the warning output says the override was 'ignored'

name: Data Analyzer: The local-only override works only in development and prints a loud warning
objective: Proves a developer can deliberately turn the protections off locally, but the script warns about it.
precondition: The container start script entrypoint.sh is run in a temporary folder with fake 'python' and 'streamlit' programs; the fake streamlit just prints the options it was given.

steps.action: Run the start script with STREAMLIT_INSECURE_LOCAL_ONLY=1 and APP_ENV=dev
steps.expected: The options show XSRF protection and CORS set to false, and the warning output contains 'OFF'

name: Data Analyzer: The old STREAMLIT_SECURE=0 setting no longer disables protection
objective: Proves a leftover legacy setting cannot weaken security.
precondition: The container start script entrypoint.sh is run in a temporary folder with fake 'python' and 'streamlit' programs; the fake streamlit just prints the options it was given.

steps.action: Run the start script with STREAMLIT_SECURE=0
steps.expected: XSRF protection is still true

name: Data Analyzer: Web page upload limit defaults to 25 MB and can be changed with a valid number
objective: Proves the upload size cap is applied, can be set to a sensible whole number, and falls back to 25 on bad values.
precondition: The container start script entrypoint.sh is run in a temporary folder with fake 'python' and 'streamlit' programs; the fake streamlit just prints the options it was given.

steps.action: Run the start script with no limit set
steps.expected: The option --server.maxUploadSize=25 is used

steps.action: Run it with a limit of 10
steps.expected: The option is --server.maxUploadSize=10

steps.action: Run it with invalid limits
steps.expected: Each falls back to --server.maxUploadSize=25

name: Data Analyzer: Streamlit settings file has protections on and a modest upload limit
objective: Proves the fixed settings file agrees with the start script.
precondition: Repository configuration files are present; they are only read.

steps.action: Read the server section of .streamlit/config.toml
steps.expected: enableXsrfProtection and enableCORS are both true, and maxUploadSize is greater than 0 and at most 100 (MB)

name: Data Analyzer: Local run script keeps protections on and listens on the local machine only
objective: Proves the developer launch script does not weaken security or expose the page to the network.
precondition: Repository configuration files are present; they are only read.

steps.action: Read run_app.sh
steps.expected: It contains neither 'enableXsrfProtection=false' nor 'enableCORS=false', and it mentions 127.0.0.1 (the local-only address)

name: Data Analyzer: Docker Compose files publish ports on the local machine only
objective: Proves none of the four Compose setups expose a port to the wider network.
precondition: Repository configuration files are present; they are only read.

steps.action: Parse each Compose file and look at every service's published ports
steps.expected: Every published port starts with '127.0.0.1:'

name: Data Analyzer: Web page container receives an explicit list of settings, not the whole secrets file
objective: Proves the page container sees only the settings it needs, so unrelated secrets such as the admin password are not passed in.
precondition: Repository configuration files are present; they are only read.

steps.action: Parse docker-compose.yml, service data-analyzer
steps.expected: It has no env_file entry; its environment includes DATA_ANALYZER_API_URL, DATA_ANALYZER_API_KEY and APP_ENV; it does not include DATA_ANALYZER_ADMIN_PASSWORD

name: Data Analyzer: Full-stack Compose setup refuses to start without an API key
objective: Proves the test rig cannot be started with an empty key, which would leave the service unprotected.
precondition: Repository configuration files are present; they are only read.

steps.action: Read docker-compose.fullstack.yml as text
steps.expected: The 'key required' form of the variable appears exactly twice and the plain no-check form does not appear

name: Data Analyzer: Old nginx example listens on port 8003 for the local machine only
objective: Proves the legacy web-server configuration does not expose port 8003 to the network.
precondition: Repository configuration files are present; they are only read.

steps.action: Read nginx-prefix-fix.conf
steps.expected: A 'listen 127.0.0.1:8003;' line is present

name: Data Analyzer: About-page diagram code makes no calls to outside websites
objective: Proves the diagram code has no web addresses, embedded scripts or third-party diagram services.
precondition: Repository configuration files are present; they are only read.

steps.action: Read mermaid_renderer.py as text
steps.expected: No 'http://' or 'https://'; no 'components.html' or '<script'; no 'mermaid.ink' or 'jsdelivr'

name: Data Analyzer: Diagram renderer shows the local picture, or falls back to showing the diagram as text
objective: Proves the About-page diagram uses a local image when it exists and plain text when it does not.
precondition: The page's display functions (image, text, caption, expander) are replaced by recorders; no browser involved.

steps.action: Render with the existing picture assets/data_flow_simple.png
steps.expected: The first thing displayed is an image

steps.action: Render with a missing picture
steps.expected: The diagram source text is displayed and no image is

name: Data Analyzer: About-page diagram pictures exist for both views
objective: Proves the two diagram pictures are present and not empty.
precondition: Repository configuration files are present; they are only read.

steps.action: Check file sizes
steps.expected: Each file is larger than 1000 bytes

name: Data Analyzer: Cache inspection script never loads pickle files
objective: Proves the helper script does not read pickle files, a format that can run attacker code when opened.
precondition: Repository configuration files are present; they are only read.

steps.action: Read scripts/inspect_cache.py as text
steps.expected: It contains no 'import pickle', no 'pickle.load', and no '.pkl' (apart from one allowed comment about '*.pkl` left')

name: Data Analyzer: Opening the About page makes no outside requests, in both diagram views
objective: Proves the rendered About page only shows pre-built diagram images served by the app and contains no embedded frames, scripts or outside image links.
precondition: The web page code is loaded in Streamlit's headless test mode with About selected; nothing is deployed or contacted.

steps.action: Render the About page, then switch the diagram choice from Simple View to Detailed View
steps.expected: Each view shows exactly one image whose address is the app's own (no http/https address), and the page has no frame, HTML-component, script, link or outside-image markup

name: Data Analyzer: Top bar tab labels are readable (contrast at least 4.5 to 1)
objective: Proves the colours set for the selected and unselected top-bar tab labels meet the WCAG 2.1 AA text contrast minimum of 4.5 to 1.
precondition: The page style rules in web_app.py are read as text; no browser is started.

steps.action: Read the label colour and background colour for the selected tab and for the unselected tab, and compute the contrast ratio
steps.data: selected: white on blue; unselected: light grey on the dark bar
steps.expected: Both ratios are 4.5 or higher (5.17 and 9.85 at the time of writing)
